newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
POLICY CHANGE MAY BOOST ILLEGAL OPIUM TRADE

The recent change in opium cultivation regulations could stimulate the illegal drugs market. The finance ministry's notification, issued on October 4, allows re-issuance of licences to opium cultivators who failed to reach the minimum qualifying yield during the 1995/96 (April-March) crop year if they undertook to fulfil requirements in the next year. This could allow opium cultivators to divert illegally their produce to the drugs market to continue in the business without any penalty. It undermined the basic idea behind the fixing of productivity norms by the government, a former finance ministry official said.
The Pioneer
LEFT PARTIES ATTACK FINANCE MINISTER

Left parties took strong exception in parliament to Finance Minister P Chidambaram's statement in a television interview hinting at a probable hike in petro-prices. The minister had committed a serious parliamentary impropriety by making such statements outside parliament, they said. The Left said the statement sent wrong signals to traders and speculators who could take advantage at the cost of consumers. The Left's stand was backed by the Bharatiya Janata Party and Congress. Chidambaram was not in the Parliament.
The Hindustan Times
RAO REFUSES TO QUIT PARTY POST

Some parliamentary members of the Congress party were reported to have demanded that former prime minister Narasimha Rao step down as Congress Parliament Party (CPP) leader. Refusing to bow to such pressure, Rao made clear he would not quit the CPP post unless MPs calling for him to go won a two-thirds majority in the CPP. Rao also called for a formal notification of the CPP elections, scheduled for December 10.
The Economic Times
CONSOLIDATION OF GROUP ACCOUNTS DEMANDED

Financial institutions (FIs) asked the finance ministry to make consolidation of accounts among group companies mandatory. The move gained momentum after the blocks faced by the institutions in deciphering the ITC group accounts and fund movements within the Tata Group. FI sources said the ministry had already accepted in principle that consolidation of group accounts ought to be made mandatory. Sources said there was a general consensus on the matter but several industry groups in the past had tried to make consolidation of group accounts optional and not mandatory.
PRIVATISATION A PRECONDITION FOR $1-BLN IBRD LOAN

The World Bank is unlikely to clear the $1 billion coal sector rehabilitation programme (CSRP) Coal India Ltd (CIL), unless steps are taken to speed up coal sector privatisation. The World Bank has expressed concern over the slow progress of the coal sector privatisation vis-a-vis the promises of the previous Congress government. The previous mining minister had promised to allow 51 percent equity participation in the coal mining projects. According to the loan plan, the Exim-Bank of Japan will chip in $500 million for the CSRP. The World Bank has already sanctioned $63 million.
BPL CELLULAR DEFERS PRICING ADR ISSUE

BPL Cellular Holdings is expected to fall short of raising $185 million to $200 million through its maiden stock floatation in the United States. It has also deferred the pricing of the American Depository Receipt issue by one week, to December 2. The company is now considering $150 million, with its shares being priced at between $10 and $12 each, compared with earlier projections of between $15 and $17 each. To reach the $150 million figure, it would also have to find buyers for its greenshoe option of an additional 15 percent equity to the 22.3 percent it wants to place.
HIGHER INPUTS COSTS SEE ACC NET SLUMP 56 PCT

Associated Cement Companies Ltd (ACC) has announced poor results for April-September. Its net profit fell 56 percent to 550 million rupees. The fall was despite an increase of about nine percent in net sales and 2.4 percent growth in production. Announcement of the results triggered a sharp fall in ACC stock to around 1,000 rupees in kerb dealings from the official closing price of 1,156 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
Financial Express
MARUTI, TELCO TOP CAR, LCV SEGMENTS

Maruti Udyog Ltd (MUL) and truck giant Telco continued their strong hold on the auto industry with sizeable market shares in October. MUL cornered a massive 82.3 percent share of the car market. Telco garnered 77.49 percent in sales in the light commercial vehicles (LCV) segment and a 67.18 percent share in the heavy commercial vehicles (HCV) segment. Premier Automobiles Ltd's share was poor at 1.2 percent. DCM Daewoo captured little over five percent of the car market. Ashok Leyland's market share was 22.18 and 0.62 percent in the LCV and the HCV segments, respectively.
EXCESSIVE RELIANCE ON ECBS MUST BE REGULATED

Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia cautioned against excessive reliance on external commercial borrowings (ECBs). He said the government would closely monitor and maintain a ceiling on ECBs as well as the flow of portfolio capital into the capital markets. The pace of opening up in these areas should not be as fast in some other areas, the finance secretary added.
CUT-OFF YIELD FOR FIVE-YEAR GILTS REDUCED

The central bank (RBI) reduced the cut-off yield for five-year government stock by 20 basis points to 13.55 percent in its 20 billion rupee auction of five-year paper. About 23 percent of the amount auctioned devolved on the RBI. The coupon for five-year stock issued earlier was pegged at 13.75 percent, while a six-year paper issue made later was fixed at 13.82 percent. There were a total of 143 bids for an amount of 23.27 billion rupees out, of which the RBI accepted 67 bids for 15.33 billion rupees at auction.
The Observer
CORPORATE EARNINGS PER SHARE DIP IN FIRST HALF

The results of the corporate sector have shown a four percent drop in earnings per share (EPS) for the six-month period ended in September, according to a study by Insight Research. The companies include leading auto companies such as Tata Electric Locomotive Company, Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra, oil majors Indian Oil Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum, steel majors Tata Iron and Steel Company, Essar Steel and Jindal Iron, besides the A.V. Birla group companies Grasim, Indian Rayon and Hindalco. A factor responsible for the fall in corporate EPSs has been an increase in equity, as well as a drop in corporate profitability, the study notes.
RBI TO END ILLEGAL CALL BACK SERVICE

The central bank's (RBI's) foreign exchange control department has indicated to all scheduled banks the RBI's intention to ban a Call Back service provided illegally for international telephone calls, faxes and modems. Payments made by any such services in the country in foreign exchange amounted to violation of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, the RBI circular said. The warning came after the matter was taken up with the RBI by the government owned international telephony, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL). VSNL had alleged such services siphoned off its revenue to foreign companies and also caused a drainage of foreign exchange.
Business Standard
GOVERNMENT SOUNDED OUT ON GUARANTEES FOR POWER PROJECTS

The government has been sounded out on a fresh set of counter-guarantees for new mega power projects. This is being touted as the immediate means to ensure fresh capacities in the light of the fact that reform of state electricity boards (SEBs) has not been on course. Officials say the underlying reason for the proposal is that the reform process at the SEBs is not taking off and this has become a barrier to foreign investments in power projects. However, this proposal is likely to face stiff opposition from the finance ministry because it entails a long-term fiscal cost, sources added.
CRR MAY BE REMOVED ON INTER-BANK TRANSACTIONS

The finance ministry has agreed in principal to a proposal to remove the cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirement on interbank loan transactions. At present, borrowings from the interbank call money market are subject to CRR requirements because they are treated as part of time and demand liabilities of a bank. The move is aimed at pushing down interest rates, which has been an area of concern for the government.
